Rashi on Nazir 30b:11:1.hebrew: בית שמאי אומרים הקדש טעות: כיצד אמר שור שחור שיצא מביתי ראשון - בשחרית יהא הקדש, ויצא לבן — הרי זה הקדש. וכן כשיעלה דינר של כסף או חבית של שמן — כולן הקדש, הואיל ויצאו בראשונה; ואף על גב שלא נתקיימו דבריו, שהוא סבור שיצא שחור, ויעלה דינר של זהב וחבית של יין תחילה:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:11:1.english: Beit Shammai say: Consecration [performed in] error: How so? If one said: "A black ox that emerges from my house first" - "[in] the morning shall be consecrated," and a white [ox] emerged — it is consecrated. And likewise, when a silver dinar or a barrel of oil comes up, all of them are consecrated, since they came out first; and even though his words were not fulfilled, for he had presumed that a black [ox] would emerge, and [that] a gold dinar and a barrel of wine would come up first.

Rashi on Nazir 30b:1:1.hebrew: קמ"ל הלכה - בן ולא בת:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:1:1.english: It teaches us [that it is] a halakha - [Specifically,] a son and not a daughter.

Rashi on Nazir 30b:2:1.hebrew: ואם תימצי לומר פליגי ארישא - הוא דפליגי רבנן, דאמרי שאף מגלח על נזירות אביו, ולא שני להו לרבנן בין רישא לסיפא, שבכולן האיש מגלח על נזירות אביו:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:2:1.english: And if you say they disagree, [is it] on the first clause - that the Rabbis disagree, as they say that [in that case] as well he shaves using his father’s naziriteship, and the Rabbis make no distinction between the first clause and the latter clause, for in all of them a man shaves using his father’s naziriteship?

Rashi on Nazir 30b:2:2.hebrew: או אסיפא פליגי - דלרבנן סבירא להו איפכא: דלמא מאי דשמיע להו מר' יוסי, דאמר ברישא דאין זה מגלח על נזירות אביו — סבירא להו לרבנן הוי מגלח; ומאי דקא"ר יוסי בסיפא דהוי מגלח — סבירא להו לרבנן דאינו מגלח:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:2:2.english: Or do they disagree on the latter clause - For according to the Rabbis they hold the opposite: perhaps that which they heard from Rabbi Yosei, who said in the first clause that this [person] does not shave on his father’s naziriteship, the Rabbis hold he shaves; and that which Rabbi Yosei says in the latter clause, that he shaves, the Rabbis hold that he does not shave.

Rashi on Nazir 30b:2:3.hebrew: ה"ג: ת"ש, כיצד אמרו האיש מגלח על נזירות אביו? מי שהיה הוא ואביו נזירים, והפריש אביו מעות לנזירות ומת — זהו שמגלח על נזירות אביו. אבל מי שהיה אביו נזיר, והפריש אביו מעות לנזירותו ומת, ואמר: "הריני נזיר על מנת שאגלח על מעות אבא" — הרי אלו יפלו לנדבה, דברי ר' יוסי. רבי אליעזר ור' מאיר ור' יהודה אומרים: זהו שמגלח על נזירות אביו - כלומר, מדקאמרי רבי אליעזר ורבי יהודה בהאיך ברייתא "זהו שמגלח", אלמא דארישא ואסיפא פליגי. והכי משמע: זהו שאמרו (ע"מ) שמגלח על נזירות אביו, אבל מי שהיה נזיר בחיי האב, שכבר נתחייב בקרבן אחד בפני עצמו — אין מגלח על נזירות אביו. ושמע מינה דארישא וסיפא פליגי. ש"מ:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:2:3.english: This is the correct version of the text: "Come and hear: How did they say that a man shaves on his father's naziriteship? One where he and his father were nazirites, and his father set aside money for his naziriteship and died — this is the one who shaves on his father's naziriteship. But one whose father was a nazirite, and his father set aside money for his naziriteship and died, and [the son] said: 'I am hereby a nazirite on the condition that I shave on father's money' — these [coins] shall fall [to the Temple treasury] for a freewill offering; [this is] the statement of Rabbi Yosei. Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Meir, and Rabbi Yehuda say: This is the one who shaves on his father's naziriteship" - That is to say, since Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehuda say in that baraita, "This is the one who shaves," it follows that they disagree with [both] the first clause and the latter clause. And this is what it means: This is the one [about whom] they said [that one who took the vow] on condition shaves on his father's naziriteship, but one who was a nazirite during his father's lifetime, who has already become obligated in an offering of his own, does not shave on his father's naziriteship. And conclude from this that they disagree with [both] the first clause and the latter clause. Conclude from this [that it is so].

Rashi on Nazir 30b:5:1.hebrew: כל דקדים - נזירותיה, מגלח על נזירות אביו. או דילמא, ירושה גמירי לה, וכל מאן דהוי בר ירושה — גמירי לה דזכי בהו:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:5:1.english: Whoever precedes - [Whichever son whose] naziriteship was earlier shaves using [the money for] his father’s naziriteship. Or perhaps we learned it as [a matter of] inheritance, and anyone who is an heir, we learned that he acquires [a share] in them.

Rashi on Nazir 30b:5:2.hebrew: ופלגא הוי כו' - וחולקין אותו בשוה: זה יביא חציו וזה חציו, ומייתו מבתיהן כדי להשלים קרבנותיהן עם מעות אביהן:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:5:2.english: And it is a half, etc. - And they divide it equally: this one brings half of it and that one half of it, and they bring [the remainder] from their homes to complete their offerings along with their father's money.

Rashi on Nazir 30b:6:1.hebrew: בעי רבא - היו לו בנים נזירין, בכור ופשוט, לגלח על נזירות אביו — היכי שקלי ביה:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:6:1.english: Rava raised a dilemma - [If] he had sons who were nazirites, a firstborn and an ordinary [son], to shave upon their father's naziriteship — how do they take from it?

Rashi on Nazir 30b:6:2.hebrew: הילכתא גמירי לה - שמגלחין על נזירות אביהן, ולא מחמת ירושה, והילכך לא בעי לגלוחי לפום מאי דשקיל, אלא בפלגא. או דילמא, ירושה היא שמגלחין בנזירות אביהן, וכי היכי דשקיל האי בכור פי שנים בכל הנכסים — הכי בהאי נמי מגלח פי שנים:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:6:2.english: We learned it as a halakha - That they shave [using the money] for their father's naziriteship, and not by virtue of inheritance; and therefore he does not need to shave in accordance with what he receives [as an inheritance], but rather with half [the money]. Or perhaps it is [by virtue of] inheritance that they shave [using the money] for their father's naziriteship, and just as this firstborn takes a double portion of all the property, so too with this [money] as well, he shaves [with] a double portion.

Rashi on Nazir 30b:7:1.english: And it is in non-sacred [property] that he has - The firstborn [has] a double portion.

Rashi on Nazir 30b:7:2.hebrew: אבל בהקדש - לאחר שנקרב הקרבן ומבקשין לאוכלו, לא שקיל פי שנים, אלא חולקין ביניהם בשוה:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:7:2.english: But with regard to consecrated [property] - After the offering has been sacrificed and they wish to eat it, he does not take a double portion, but rather they divide [it] equally among themselves.

Rashi on Nazir 30b:7:3.hebrew: או דילמא - כי היכי דקני ליה פי שנים לגלח בהן, הכי נמי לענין חלוקה לאחר שהקריבו קרבנותיהן, אע"ג דמוקדשין הן, שקיל בהו פי שנים:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:7:3.english: Or perhaps - Just as he acquires a double portion to shave with them, so too regarding the division [of the meat] after they have sacrificed their offerings, even though they are consecrated [items], he takes a double portion in them.

Rashi on Nazir 30b:8:1.hebrew: כי גמירי הילכתא בסתם נזירות - היכא דתרוייהו קיימי בסתם נזירות, אבל היכא דחד מנהון נזיר עולם — לא; או דילמא לא שנא:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:8:1.english: When the halakha was learned, [it was] regarding an unspecified naziriteship - Where both of them are in [a state of] unspecified naziriteship, but where one of them is a permanent nazirite, [it does] not [apply]; or perhaps it is no different?

Rashi on Nazir 30b:9:1.hebrew: ואת"ל הכא - כיון דנזירות דאבא ונזירות דברא נזירות דטהרה הוא, מגלח הבן על נזירות האב:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:9:1.english: And if you say: Here - Since the father’s naziriteship and the son’s naziriteship are [both] a naziriteship of purity, the son shaves on his father’s naziriteship:

Rashi on Nazir 30b:9:2.hebrew: בעי רב אשי היכא דאביו נזיר טמא והוא נזיר טהור - מהו להוסיף על מעות צפורין שהפריש אביו, להביא בהן קרבנות? וכן, אם אביו טהור והוא טמא, מהו להביא צפורים באותן מעות שהפריש אביו לנזירות טהרתו? תיקו:
Rashi on Nazir 30b:9:2.english: Rav Ashi raises a dilemma: Where his father was an impure nazirite and he was a pure nazirite - What is [the halakha]: May he add to the money for the birds that his father designated, to bring sacrifices with them? And likewise, if his father was pure and he is impure, what is [the halakha]: May he bring birds with that money that his father designated for the naziriteship of his purity? [The dilemma] stands [unresolved].

Tosafot on Nazir 30b:11:1.hebrew: בית שמאי אומרים הקדש טעות הוי הקדש - כדמפרש ואזיל. ומשום דבתר הכי איירי בנזירות בטעות, נקט הני פלוגתייהו במכילתין; וכן משום פלוגתא דבית שמאי ובית הלל דבסמוך, גבי ״מי שנדר ונשאל לחכמים״ כו׳, אמרו להם בית הלל לבית שמאי: ״אי אתם מודים בזה שהוא הקדש טעות, ותצא ותרעה בעדר?״ — כלומר: אם כן, [היאך] אומרים בהקדש טעות דפליגי עלן:
Tosafot on Nazir 30b:11:1.english: Beit Shammai say: Erroneous consecration is consecration - As [the Mishnah] goes on to explain. And because afterwards [the chapter] deals with naziriteship [undertaken] in error, [the Tanna] cited these disputes of theirs in our tractate. And also because of the dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel nearby, regarding "One who took a vow and consulted the Sages, etc.," [where] Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai: "Do you not concede in this [case] that it is an erroneous consecration, and it shall go out and graze among the flock?" — that is to say: If so, [how] do they say regarding erroneous consecration that they disagree with us?

Tosafot on Nazir 30b:2:1.hebrew: אם תימצי לומר פליגי - רבנן עליה דר' יוסי — מדקתני במתני' "ר' יוסי אומר", משמע דפליגי רבנן עליה. ואם תימצי לומר פליגי רבנן: ארישא — דקאמר ר' יוסי: אם נדר בחיי אביו אינו מגלח, ואמרי רבנן דמגלח בכל ענין; [או] אסיפא — דקאמר: דנדר לאחר מיתה מגלח על [נזירות] אביו, ואמרי רבנן אינו מגלח:
Tosafot on Nazir 30b:2:1.english: "If you say they disagree" - [Regarding whether] the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Yosei — since it teaches in the Mishnah, "Rabbi Yosei says," this implies that the Rabbis disagree with him. And if you say that the Rabbis disagree: [Is it] on the first clause — where Rabbi Yosei says that if he vowed during his father's lifetime he does not shave [using his father's offerings], and the Rabbis say that he shaves in any case; [or] on the latter clause — where he says that [if] he vowed after [his father's] death he shaves by using his father's [naziriteship], and the Rabbis say he does not shave?

Tosafot on Nazir 30b:2:2.hebrew: תא שמע - דארישא פליגי, דתניא: כיצד אמרו: "האיש מגלח על מעות אביו"? מי שהיה אביו נזיר והפריש אביו מעות לנזירותו ומת, ואמר: "הריני נזיר ע"מ שאגלח על מעות אביו" — אבל מי שהיה הוא ואביו נזירים והפריש אביו מעות לנזירותו ומת, הרי אלו יפלו לנדבה, דברי רבי יוסי. ר"א ור' מאיר ור' יהודה אומרים: "זהו שמגלח על נזירות אביו". וברוב ספרים היא משובשת:
Tosafot on Nazir 30b:2:2.english: Come and hear - [Proof] that they disagree on the first clause, for it was taught [in a baraita]: "How did they say that a man shaves using his father’s money? One whose father was a nazirite, and his father separated money for his naziriteship and died, and [the son] said: 'I am hereby a nazirite on the condition that I can shave using my father’s money' — but one where he and his father were [both] nazirites, and his father separated money for his naziriteship and died, these [funds] shall be allocated for gift-offerings; [this is] the statement of Rabbi Yosei. Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Meir, and Rabbi Yehuda say: This is the one who shaves using his father’s naziriteship." And in most books it is corrupted.

Tosafot on Nazir 30b:5:1.hebrew: בעי רבה יש לו שני בנים נזירים - לרבי יוסי, שנדרו אחר מיתת אביהן; ולרבנן, גם בחיי אביהן:
Tosafot on Nazir 30b:5:1.english: Rabba raised a dilemma: If he has two nazirite sons - According to Rabbi Yose, [this is a case where] they vowed after their father’s death; and according to the Rabbis, even during their father’s lifetime.

Tosafot on Nazir 30b:5:2.hebrew: הילכתא גמירי לה - [ולא] כדין חלוקה בשוה. "וכל דקדם גלח" — וכל הקודם מהם זכה בהם:
Tosafot on Nazir 30b:5:2.english: "We learned it as a halakha" - [And not] according to the law of equal division. And "whoever precedes shaves" — whichever of them comes first acquires them [the funds].

Tosafot on Nazir 30b:5:3.hebrew: ופלגא הוי - פלגא: זה נוטל החצי וזה נוטל החצי, כמו בשאר ירושה:
Tosafot on Nazir 30b:5:3.english: "And is it a half?" - [Meaning] a half: this one takes half and that one takes half, as in any other inheritance.

Tosafot on Nazir 30b:6:1.hebrew: בעי [רבא] - גריס ר"ת, והראשון [רבה בכור] ופשוט נזירים מהו: הלכתא גמירי לה — ולא מן הדין, והכא לא בעי גלוחי לפום מאי דשקיל; דאע"פ דשני פשוטי פלגי, מכל מקום אינו כשאר ירושה; ה"נ לענין שיטול הבכור פי שנים, [וה"נ] לא מצי להביא תגלחתו לפום מאי דשקיל כשאר נכסים? או דילמא: ירושה גמירי — כי היכי [דנוטל] פי שנים ממעות שהפריש אביו לקרבנות נזירותו, [כן מגלח]? ואת"ל: בחולין הוא דאית ליה פי שנים — פי' ר"ת: בחולין, דאמר לשון חולין ולא לשון הקדש, דאמר "מעות אלו לנזירות"; [אבל] בהקדש לא — אילו אמר "הרי אלו לקרבנות נזירותו":
Tosafot on Nazir 30b:6:1.english: "Rava raised a dilemma" - Rabbeinu Tam reads [here "Rava"], and [in] the first [dilemma, "Rabbah"]. [Regarding] a firstborn and an ordinary [son who are both] nazirites, what is [the ruling]? [Is it that] we learned it as a halakha, and not by [the standard legal] law, and therefore he does not need to shave in accordance with what he receives — for even though two ordinary [sons] divide [the money], nevertheless it is not like other inheritance; so too regarding the firstborn taking a double portion, [so too] he cannot bring his shaving [offerings] in accordance with what he receives like other property? Or perhaps we learned it as [a matter of] inheritance, [and] just as [he takes] a double portion of the money that his father designated for his nazirite offerings, [so does he shave]? And if you say: It is [only] with regard to non-sacred property that he has a double portion — Rabbeinu Tam explains: "With regard to non-sacred property" [means] where he used non-sacred terminology and not the terminology of consecration, as when he said, "These funds are for nezirut"; [but] with regard to consecrated property he does not, which would be if he had said, "These [funds] are hereby for my nazirite offerings."

Tosafot on Nazir 30b:7:1.hebrew: או דילמא כיון [דקני] ליה לגלוחי לא שנא - ואפילו אמר "לקרבנות נזירותו", דמוכח לשון הקדש:
Tosafot on Nazir 30b:7:1.english: "Or perhaps, since he [acquired] it for shaving, it is no different" - And [this is so] even if [the father] said: "For the offerings of his naziriteship", where the wording clearly indicates consecration.

Tosafot on Nazir 30b:8:1.hebrew: אביו נזיר עולם והוא נזיר סתם - או איפכא. כי גמירי הלכתא בסתם נזיר — ומצי למיבעי: דאביו והוא נזיר עולם? או שמא הא פשיטא דמגלח, כיון ששמו האב והבן בחד גוונא לנזירות? ואת"ל: הכא אידי ואידי בנזירות טהרה, ומגלח שפיר על מעות אביו:
Tosafot on Nazir 30b:8:1.english: "His father was a permanent nazirite and he was an unspecified nazirite" - Or the reverse. [Regarding the Gemara's rationale:] "When we learned the halakha, [did we learn it only] regarding an unspecified nazirite?" — and [the Gemara] could have raised the dilemma [even where both] his father and he were permanent nazirites! Or perhaps this is obvious that he shaves, since the father and the son are classified in one [and the same] type of naziriteship? And if you say [as the Gemara continues]: Here, both this and that are naziriteship of purity, and [therefore] he may well shave using his father's money.

Tosafot on Nazir 30b:9:1.hebrew: בעי רב אשי אביו נזיר טמא והוא נזיר טהור - אביו נזיר טמא: נטמא והפריש מעות לציפורים ואשם — מהו שיוסיף בנו על אותם מעות להביא חטאת, עולה, ושלמים לנזירות טהרה? אי נמי: אביו נזיר טמא, וחזר והתחיל ומנה נזירות טהרה — הואיל ונטמא, לא הוי דומיא דנזירות דבן דלא נטמא; לא מגלח? אביו נזיר טהור והפריש מעות, והוא נזיר טמא — מהו שיביא הבן צפורים [מן] המעות שהפריש אביו לנזירות טהרה:
Tosafot on Nazir 30b:9:1.english: Rav Ashi raises a dilemma: [If] his father was an impure nazirite and he was a pure nazirite - "[If] his father was an impure nazirite" — [meaning,] he became defiled and set aside money for birds and a guilt offering; what is [the halakha as to] whether his son may add to those funds to bring a sin offering, a burnt offering, and peace offerings for a naziriteship of purity? Alternatively: His father was an impure nazirite and [subsequently] went back, started [over], and counted a naziriteship of purity — since [the father] became defiled, [his naziriteship] is not comparable to the naziriteship of the son who did not become defiled; [does he therefore] not shave? [If] his father was a pure nazirite and set aside money, and he was an impure nazirite — what is [the halakha as to] whether the son may bring birds [from] the money that his father set aside for a naziriteship of purity?
